title: Target users 'existing' / 'affiliates' / 'segment' are written but never enforced — anyone can redeem the code
detail: The Target users Select offers all/new/existing/affiliates/segment (TARGET_OPTIONS, lines 32-38) and writes `targetUsers` verbatim (api/coupons.ts:131). The only server enforcement of any target is the derived `firstOrderOnly` flag (i.e. 'new'). `computeCouponDiscount` in functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:143-203 — the path used when a customer types a code — never reads `targetUsers`, and neither does the authoritative re-validation inside the placeOrder transaction (checkout.ts:505-525). `targetUsers` is only consulted to EXCLUDE a coupon from auto-apply (checkout.ts:263, web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:53/144, app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:101). There is also no segment definition anywhere in the codebase, so 'segment' is meaningless.
failure_scenario: Admin creates AFFILIATE20, 20% off, Target users = 'Affiliates', intending it for the affiliate network only. A regular shopper is told the code by a friend, types AFFILIATE20 in the bag, and applyCoupon/placeOrder grant the full 20% — no check of targetUsers happens on the code-entry path. Same for an 'Existing users' coupon redeemed by a brand-new signup.
fix: Either enforce targetUsers in computeCouponDiscount (look up customers/{uid}.stats.ordersCount for 'existing', the affiliates collection for 'affiliates') or cut the unenforceable options down to the two that actually work ('all', 'new') until segments exist.

verdict.reason: Verified and could not refute. admin/src/features/coupons/routes/CouponFormPage.tsx:32-38 and 317-323 expose Target users = all|new|existing|affiliates|segment, and admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:131-132 persists targetUsers verbatim while deriving only firstOrderOnly for 'new'. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts computeCouponDiscount (~155-225, the applyCoupon/manual-code path) checks active, status, validFrom/validUntil, minCartValuePaise, maxUsesTotal, maxUsesPerUser, firstOrderOnly and applicableCategories but never reads targetUsers; the authoritative in-transaction re-assert at checkout.ts:573-591 likewise omits it. The only readers of targetUsers repo-wide are auto-apply/offer-list exclusions (checkout.ts:283, web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:53 and :144, app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:101), all of the form "if !== all then skip". A "visibility-only by design" defence fails: where that IS the intent the code says so explicitly (offers.ts:65-71 and checkout.ts:295-300 comment that firstOrderOnly/maxUsesPerUser coupons are hidden from auto-apply because typing the code still validates fully server-side) — there is no such server validation for targetUsers, and autoApply already exists as a separate field checked one line away (checkout.ts:284). targetUsers is a required field on the shared Coupon type (packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:39), so it is not vestigial. A repo-wide grep finds no customer-segment concept whatsoever, so 'segment' is unresolvable; and grep for coupon over functions/src/affiliate/*.ts returns nothing, so 'affiliates' has no enforcement anywhere. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and it is the direct sibling of the already-fixed applicableCategories defect. Impact is real money: an Affiliates or Existing-users code shared with anyone is honoured in full by applyCoupon and placeOrder. Fixable by mirroring the firstOrderOnly guard (existing => stats.ordersCount > 0; affiliates => affiliates/{uid} exists) in both computeCouponDiscount and the placeOrder re-assert, and dropping 'segment' from TARGET_OPTIONS until a segment model exists.

title: Category restriction is written but ignored by the web (and mostly by the app) offer list, advertising discounts the server refuses
detail: The admin writes `applicableCategories` as category slugs (CouponFormPage.tsx:328-343, api/coupons.ts:130) and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:114-119 correctly restricts the discount to matching `product.categorySlug` lines. The web mirror does not: `PromoCoupon` (offers.ts:31-47) does not even declare applicableCategories, `promoDiscount` (lines 50-79) computes the discount over the whole subtotal, and `listAvailableOffers` (lines 141-158) prints the sub-line as 'On any order' / 'Min cart X'. The app (app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:107-111) only hints at the restriction when exactly one category is selected and still computes the discount over the full subtotal.
failure_scenario: Admin creates SWEETS20 (20% off, capped Rs.200) and taps only the 'Sweets' chip. A customer with a bag of only Dry Fruits opens checkout: the offers list shows 'SWEETS20 - 20% off, up to Rs.200 - On any order' as a qualifying offer. Tapping it applies it, then the applyCoupon re-validation returns failed-precondition ('This coupon does not apply to the items in your bag'), the coupon is torn back off and an error toast fires. For a mixed bag the headline discount is inflated versus what the server actually grants.
fix: Add `applicableCategories` to PromoCoupon and mirror `discountableSubtotal` in offers.ts (and offers.dart), filtering cart lines by categorySlug before computing the discount and the qualifies/shortfall values.

verdict.reason: Verified real. `applicableCategories` is written by the admin as category slugs (admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts saveCoupon, chips keyed by c.slug in CouponFormPage.tsx) and is enforced server-side by discountableSubtotal in functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:134-140, used by both computeCouponDiscount (lines 205-208, 235-238) and autoBestOffer (line ~305), throwing failed-precondition 'This coupon does not apply to the items in your bag.' A repo-wide grep for `applicableCategories` hits only packages/shared, admin, functions and scripts/seed.ts — nothing under web/. web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts PromoCoupon (31-48) omits the field, promoDiscount ignores it, and listAvailableOffers (141-161) labels such a coupon 'On any order'/'Min cart X' with qualifies = subtotal >= min, so checkout/page.tsx:567-577 renders an active Apply button. Tapping it calls applyOffer, the revalidation effect (page.tsx:190-213) calls applyCoupon, the server rejects, the coupon is torn back off and an error toast fires — a reachable, user-visible cross-surface mismatch, not covered by the ALREADY-FIXED entry (which is server-side only) or the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. Two caveats that reduce severity but not validity: (1) the 'inflated discount' half is largely unreachable for admin-authored promos because saveCoupon always writes maxUsesPerUser: 1 and offers.ts:70 forces promoDiscount to 0, so bestOfferForCart never auto-applies them; (2) personal/spin coupons never carry applicableCategories (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:159-171), so only the promo list path misleads. Fix is feasible: declare the field on PromoCoupon, show 'Sweets only' in the sub-line and stop marking/auto-applying it as qualifying (the web cart line lacks categorySlug — web/src/lib/cart.ts:7-17 — so full client-side filtering needs the slug added to CartLine).

title: Free-shipping coupons are auto-applied on web regardless of target users, expiry or min cart
detail: `bestOfferForCart` calls `consider(c.code, promoDiscount(...), c.discountType === 'free_shipping')` and `consider` treats `waiveDelivery` alone as 'better' (line 200: `const better = discountPaise > 0 || waiveDelivery;`). All of promoDiscount's rejection rules — targetUsers != 'all' (line 53), validUntil past (line 58), min cart not met (line 60), usage limit exhausted (line 64) — only zero the *discount*, which is already 0 for free shipping. The waiveDelivery flag survives every one of them, so the coupon wins auto-apply. Because the server code-entry path also never checks targetUsers, the subsequent applyCoupon re-validation accepts it.
failure_scenario: Admin creates FREESHIPAFF, discount type 'Free shipping', Target users = 'Affiliates'. Every ordinary web customer who opens checkout sees the toast 'Best offer applied - FREESHIPAFF' and gets delivery waived; placeOrder honours it because computeCouponDiscount only checks active/status/validity, not targetUsers. The admin's targeting is completely bypassed and the store eats the delivery cost on every order. The same path also lets a min-cart-Rs.999 free-shipping coupon apply to a Rs.100 cart.
fix: Have promoDiscount return an eligibility flag (or a `{discountPaise, waiveDelivery}` pair) so the targetUsers / validity / minimum / usage rejections zero waiveDelivery too, and pass that flag into `consider`.

verdict.reason: Real, reachable defect. In web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts, bestOfferForCart (line 206) computes waiveDelivery straight off the raw coupon doc, independently of promoDiscount, and consider() (line 200: `discountPaise > 0 || waiveDelivery`) treats that flag alone as sufficient to auto-apply. Every promoDiscount rejection (targetUsers != 'all' L53, autoApply false L54, validFrom/validUntil L56-59, minCartValuePaise L61, maxUsesTotal L64) only zeroes the discount, which is already 0 for free_shipping, so all of them are bypassed for that coupon class. listAvailableOffers (L141-148) pre-filters those same conditions correctly, showing the omission is unintended rather than by design. Reachability verified end-to-end: checkout page.tsx:162 queries `coupons` with only where('status','==','active') and no targetUsers filter; firestore.rules:74 lets any signed-in user read /coupons/{id}; the admin form genuinely writes both discountType 'free_shipping' (CouponFormPage.tsx:30/161) and targetUsers 'affiliates' (COUPON_TARGETS, enums.ts:81). Server does not rescue it: the auto-applied code is sent as couponCode (page.tsx:315) so placeOrder (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:454) uses computeCouponDiscount, whose promo branch (L171-223) checks active/status/validity/minCart/usage/firstOrderOnly/categories but never targetUsers, then sets waiveDelivery=true (L212) and summarise zeroes delivery (L367). Notably the server's own autoBestOffer DOES check targetUsers (L283), which is why the gap only shows on the explicit-code path. Two sub-claims are overstated but do not refute: the min-cart and expired cases are caught by computeCouponDiscount and cleared by the client revalidation effect (page.tsx:185-217), degrading to a spurious 'Best offer applied' toast then an error. The targetUsers bypass is unmitigated anywhere and yields placed orders with delivery waived. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists.

title: Approve & pay never checks the confirmed balance — admin can pay out more than the affiliate has earned
detail: `requestWithdrawal` validates `amountPaise > confirmed` only at REQUEST time (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:41). `approveWithdrawal` re-reads the customer inside the transaction but never re-validates: line 108 takes `amount = w.requestedAmountPaise`, line 115 does `Math.max(0, confirmed - amount)` (silently flooring at zero) and line 117 adds the FULL `amount` to `withdrawnBalancePaise`. The admin UI likewise renders the Confirmed column (admin/src/features/affiliate/routes/AffiliateListPage.tsx:170) purely as decoration — `doApprove` (line 99) never compares `confirmedOf(w)` with `w.requestedAmountPaise`, and the Approve button is never disabled. Meanwhile `reverseCommissionsForRefund` (functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:150-176) legitimately decrements `confirmedBalancePaise` while a request is open.
failure_scenario: Affiliate requests ₹5,000 while confirmed = ₹5,000. Before the admin acts, a referred order is returned and approved, clawing back ₹2,000 → confirmed = ₹3,000. Admin opens /affiliate, sees Confirmed ₹3,000 next to Amount ₹5,000, clicks Approve & pay. The CF succeeds: confirmed floors to 0, withdrawnBalancePaise jumps by ₹5,000, the request is marked paid, and the admin manually transfers ₹5,000 for ₹3,000 of earned commission. Ledger totals (confirmed + withdrawn vs lifetime) are now permanently inconsistent and nothing flags it.
fix: In the transaction, throw `failed-precondition` when `amount > (aff.confirmedBalancePaise ?? 0)`, and mirror it client-side by disabling Approve (with an inline 'insufficient confirmed balance' hint) when `confirmedOf(w) < w.requestedAmountPaise`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect. functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:103-127 (approveWithdrawal) re-reads the customer doc inside the transaction yet its only precondition is the request status; line 115 does Math.max(0, confirmed - amount) (silently flooring) and line 117 adds the FULL amount to withdrawnBalancePaise, with no comparison of amount against confirmedBalancePaise. The only balance validation in the entire codebase is at request time (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:39-40), and that file's own header states the confirmed balance is deducted only on admin approval, so the check is inherently stale. The claimed race is real: functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:149-174 decrements affiliate.confirmedBalancePaise for confirmed commission rows on an approved return, and nothing in that path checks or blocks on hasPendingWithdrawal. Grepping confirmedBalancePaise and approveWithdrawal across functions/, admin/, web/, app/ and packages/shared shows no other server-side guard; the admin wrapper (admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts:46) is a bare httpsCallable passthrough. The admin UI confirms the cosmetic-only claim: confirmedOf(w) is rendered at AffiliateListPage.tsx:170 but doApprove (line 99) never compares it to requestedAmountPaise, the Approve button (line 175) is never disabled, and the dialog text at lines 201-204 asserts a deduction from confirmed commission that does not fully happen. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (that entry covers reversal existing, which is the mechanism creating this window) and not KNOWN-INTENTIONAL (manual payouts being deliberate makes the over-approval worse, since 'paid' is the admin's cue to wire real money). Also asymmetric with the reversal path, which deliberately records unrecoveredPaise rather than silently absorbing a shortfall. Fix: re-validate amount <= confirmedBalancePaise inside the existing transaction and gate the Approve button in the UI.

title: Approve dialog promises the gross amount; the affiliate is only ever paid netPayoutPaise
detail: `requestWithdrawal` computes `processingFeePaise` from settings/affiliate and stores `netPayoutPaise = amount - fee` on the request (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:49-68). The web withdraw screen shows the affiliate 'You receive {net}' (web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:186) and the activity list debits `w.netPayoutPaise` (web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/page.tsx:80). The admin panel never reads `netPayoutPaise` or `processingFeePaise` anywhere: the table Amount column (line 172) and the confirm dialog body ('{X} will be transferred to … bank', line 196) both use `requestedAmountPaise`. Since payouts are executed by hand off exactly this number, the admin transfers the gross figure.
failure_scenario: Ops sets settings/affiliate.processingFeeType='percent', processingFeeValue=2. Affiliate withdraws ₹10,000 → request stores processingFee ₹200, netPayout ₹9,800, and the affiliate's app says 'You receive ₹9,800'. Admin sees only '₹10,000 will be transferred to Ramesh's HDFC ••4821' and NEFTs ₹10,000 — the business silently eats the fee on every payout, and the admin's screen and the customer's screen disagree about the paid amount.
fix: Show `processingFeePaise` and `netPayoutPaise` in the withdrawals table and make the confirm dialog read 'Transfer {netPayoutPaise} (₹{requested} less {fee} fee)'.

verdict.reason: The claim holds. functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:49-51,67-68 stores processingFeePaise and netPayoutPaise on each withdrawalRequests doc; web (web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:41-42,183-187) and the Flutter app (app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_repository.dart:25-33) both compute and promise the affiliate the NET amount. A repo-wide grep for netPayoutPaise|processingFeePaise returns zero hits under admin/: AffiliateListPage.tsx renders requestedAmountPaise in the Amount cell (line 172), the approve dialog body ('{X} will be transferred to …bank', line 196) and the 'pending payout' header stat (line 54). Since affiliate payouts are deliberately manual, that dialog number is exactly what ops transfers, so with a non-zero fee the business overpays and admin/customer screens disagree. Refutation attempts failed: no server-side recompute at approval (approveWithdrawal, functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:107,116-118, deducts the gross from confirmedBalancePaise — consistent with the affiliate absorbing the fee, which makes the admin copy the outlier), no other admin route shows net, field is not dead, and it is not on the fixed/intentional lists. Mitigation (hence medium, not high): the fee is 0 in both seed.ts:207-208 and bootstrap-real.ts:116 and admin has no UI writing settings/affiliate (useAffiliate() in admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:25-27 is unused), so the defect is latent until ops sets a non-zero fee in the settings doc that web/app already read live. Fix is a one-liner: show netPayoutPaise (and the fee) in the table and dialog.

title: Moderating one review overwrites the product's whole rating aggregate — wiping admin-entered / seeded ratings
detail: adminModerateReview recomputes products/{id}.rating + ratingCount purely from the `reviews` docs whose status == 'approved' (lines 70-91) and writes the result on EVERY decision, including a reject of a review that was only 'pending' and therefore never contributed to the aggregate. But the admin product form deliberately lets an operator type rating/ratingCount by hand (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:405-431, saved at :217-222 with the explicit comment that it must not clobber moderation), and the seeder ships every product with rating 4 + i/10 and ratingCount 10 + i*3 (/home/h/barkath/scripts/seed.ts:382-383) with zero review documents behind them. The first moderation action on any product therefore replaces that number with the count of real approved review docs — usually 0 or 1. Nothing warns the admin; the confirm dialog only says the review 'will go live … and update its rating'.
failure_scenario: Admin opens Reviews ▸ Pending, sees one spam review on 'Amber Oud EDP' (product card currently shows 4.0 ★ · 10 ratings) and clicks Reject → confirm. The CF flips the review to rejected AND writes ratingCount: 0, rating: 0 on products/1. On web (ProductCard.tsx:119, ProductDetail.tsx:193) and in the app (product_details_screen.dart:188/329) the gate is `ratingCount > 0`, so the product's star rating disappears from every card and the PDP. Rejecting a spam review silently deleted the product's rating, and there is no undo in the admin UI.
fix: Only touch the aggregate when the review actually enters or leaves the 'approved' set (skip the product write entirely for pending→rejected), and either drop the manual rating/ratingCount inputs from the product form or seed real review docs so the recompute cannot destroy a number no review can reproduce.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. functions/src/reviews/moderation.ts:82-91 writes products/{id}.rating + ratingCount from the approved-review set on any status change where the product exists, with no guard for decisions that don't alter that set. A pending->rejected transition (the review never contributed) therefore overwrites the aggregate with 0/0 when no approved review docs exist. Manual aggregates are a supported production feature, not just seed data: admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:401-431 exposes the fields and :213-222 deliberately omits them from the patch unless edited so as not to clobber moderation, i.e. the two are meant to coexist. The admin contract explicitly expects a reject to 'take back the rating it contributed, if any' (admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:45) and the reject confirm dialog never mentions the product rating. firestore.rules:122-141 makes reviews client-immutable and customer-created as 'pending', so this CF is the only writer besides the product form; nothing in web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared compensates. Customer impact confirmed: ratingCount > 0 gates the star display in web ProductCard.tsx:119, ProductDetail.tsx:193, wishlist page:116 and app product_card.dart:94, product_details_screen.dart:188/329. Claim overstates slightly ('EVERY decision' — line 61 no-ops an identical status, and the write is skipped when the product doc is missing), and moderation.ts:9-11 arguably intends to override hand-edited ratings, which is why confidence is medium rather than high; but that intent cannot justify a destructive write on a transition that changes nothing. Minimal fix: skip the product update when neither the previous nor the new status is 'approved'.

title: An approved or rejected review can never be re-moderated — no un-publish path exists anywhere
detail: The Action cell renders Approve/Reject buttons only when `tab === 'pending'`; on the Approved and Rejected tabs it renders a static <Badge> (lines 148-157). There is no row menu, no bulk action and no detail view. firestore.rules:123 sets `allow update, delete: if false` on reviews for every client including admins, so the only possible path is the adminModerateReview callable — which does support flipping either direction (Payload accepts 'approved'|'rejected' and the stored-status guard at moderation.ts:59 only no-ops on an identical status). The UI simply never offers it, so a decision is irreversible from the admin panel.
failure_scenario: Admin approves a 5-star review, then a customer complains it contains a competitor's phone number / abusive text. The admin opens Reviews ▸ Approved, finds the review, and there is nothing to click — only a green 'Published' badge. The review stays live on the web PDP and the app forever; the only remedy is a manual Firestore console edit (which rules also forbid from the client SDK).
fix: Render 'Unpublish' on the Approved tab (call adminModerateReview with status 'rejected') and 'Publish' on the Rejected tab, reusing the existing confirm dialogs.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. ReviewsListPage.tsx:147-158 renders Approve/Reject only when tab === 'pending'; the Approved and Rejected tabs render a static Badge with no row menu, bulk action or detail route, and a grep of admin/src shows this page (router.tsx:85, /reviews) is the ONLY reviews surface in the panel. firestore.rules:141 sets `allow update, delete: if false` on /reviews/{id} with an explicit comment that no client, admin included, may update a review directly, so no fallback path exists. Meanwhile the backend fully supports the reverse flip: functions/src/reviews/moderation.ts Payload accepts 'approved'|'rejected' with no 'must be pending' precondition, the guard at line 61 only no-ops on an identical stored status, and line 87 explicitly handles rejecting a previously-approved review by dropping it from the approved set and recomputing products/{id}.rating + ratingCount (audit action review.rejected included). So an abusive review that was approved can never be taken down from the admin panel even though the callable and rules were designed for it. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry only covers the callable existing for reviews-only sub-admins) and not on the known-intentional list. Fix is UI-only: offer the opposite action on the Approved/Rejected tabs reusing the existing setApprove/setReject confirm dialogs.

title: getCoupon rejection is unhandled — deep-linking an edit page can hang on the spinner forever
detail: `getCoupon(routeId!).then(...)` has no `.catch`, and `setLoading(false)` lives only inside the fulfilled branch (line 111). `loading` is initialised to `!isNew && !seed` (line 65), so on a cold cache (hard refresh or a pasted URL) the page renders only the Spinner (lines 187-193). Any rejection — offline, a rules denial, a transient Firestore error — leaves the component stuck on the spinner and produces an unhandled promise rejection. There is no error UI and no retry.
failure_scenario: An admin pastes /coupons/coupon_2 into a fresh tab on a flaky connection. The getDoc rejects; the screen shows a spinning loader indefinitely with no message, no toast and no way out except the sidebar, and the console logs an uncaught rejection.
fix: Chain `.catch((e) => { toast.error('Could not load this coupon.'); navigate('/coupons'); })` (or render an inline error + Retry) and move `setLoading(false)` into a `.finally`.

verdict.reason: Claim verified line-by-line and I could not refute it. CouponFormPage.tsx:90 has no .catch and setLoading(false) exists only in the fulfilled branch (line 111); loading initialises to !isNew && !seed (line 65) where seed comes from the module-level in-memory cache in admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts, which is empty on a hard refresh or pasted URL; the loading branch (lines 187-193) renders only a Spinner with no error or retry state. Nothing handles it elsewhere: /coupons/:id is a plain deep-linkable route (admin/src/app/router.tsx:87), no route has an errorElement, there is no ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch anywhere in admin/src, and main.tsx registers no unhandledrejection handler (and an error boundary would not catch a promise rejection anyway). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Two caveats that lower severity but do not refute: the rules-denial vector is mostly unavailable because firestore.rules:74 grants coupons read to any signed-in user, so the realistic trigger is an offline/transient getDoc rejection; and the same un-caught load pattern exists in ProductFormPage.tsx:109, BannerFormPage.tsx:60 and CategoryFormPage.tsx:54, making this a systemic robustness gap rather than a coupon-specific regression. The admin can still leave via the sidebar, so it is a stuck-view/no-feedback defect, not data loss. Real and trivially fixable (catch -> setLoading(false) + error UI), so refuted=false at medium confidence given the modest severity.

title: Usage limit accepts 0 (and fractions), producing a coupon that is dead on arrival
detail: The Usage limit input (lines 281-288) has no validation entry in `FormErrors` and `onSave` maps it as `maxUsesTotal: usageLimit === '' ? null : Number(usageLimit)` — only an empty string means unlimited. A typed 0 is stored as 0. Server side, functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:164-166 does `const maxTotal = c.maxUsesTotal == null ? null : Number(c.maxUsesTotal); if (maxTotal !== null && Number(c.usesCount ?? 0) >= maxTotal) throw 'This coupon has reached its usage limit.'` — with maxTotal 0 and usesCount 0 that is `0 >= 0`, always true. The same comparison in web/offers.ts:64 and checkout.ts:275/513 also hides it from every offer list. Fractional and negative values typed into the number input are likewise stored unvalidated.
failure_scenario: Admin creates DIWALI50 and types 0 in Usage limit meaning 'no limit'. It saves with a green 'Coupon created' toast and shows Status = Active, Used = 0 in the list. Every customer who enters DIWALI50 gets 'This coupon has reached its usage limit.' and it never appears in any offer list. Nothing in the admin UI explains why.
fix: Validate the field: reject values < 1 and non-integers with an inline error, and/or treat 0 as null (unlimited) in onSave. Add a helper line saying 'Leave blank for unlimited'.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. CouponFormPage.tsx:46-51 has no FormErrors entry for the usage limit and onSave (122-156) never validates it; line 166 maps only '' to null, so a typed 0 (or 2.5, or a negative — min/step on the number input at line 404-412 are advisory, there is no form-level validity check) is stored verbatim. coupons.ts:129 writes it through unclamped and computeStatus still yields 'active'; firestore.rules:74 has no field validation. Server-side every consumer treats 0 as a hard limit rather than unlimited — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:184-187 (code entry), :294-295 (autoBestOffer), :580-583 (placeOrder) and web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:63-64 all do `maxUsesTotal == null ? null : Number(...)` then `usesCount >= maxTotal`, i.e. 0 >= 0 is always true. grep across packages/shared, web, app, functions and scripts shows no normaliser anywhere; the Flutter app never reads the field. Admin gives zero feedback: CouponsListPage.tsx:164 renders usesCount only, never the limit, and the badge stays Active. The codebase's own sibling field uses the opposite convention (checkout.ts:188 treats maxUsesPerUser 0 as unlimited), which makes '0 = no limit' a very natural admin assumption and strengthens the trap. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Real, functional (coupon is unusable and invisible in every offer list), and fixable with a validation entry.

title: 'Enable affiliate wallet access' toggle writes a field nothing reads
detail: The toggle sends `walletEnabled` to adminAllocateAffiliate, which persists it as `affiliate.walletEnabled` (functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:57 — the code comment itself says 'at least persist what the admin chose'). Grepping all four surfaces, the only other `walletEnabled` hits are settings/paymentGateway.walletEnabled (web checkout, admin PaymentGatewayTab) which is an unrelated field. Nothing gates on `affiliate.walletEnabled`: `requestWithdrawal` checks only `aff.enabled` (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:36), the web affiliate/withdraw pages check only `affiliate.enabled`, and the Flutter AffiliateInfo model (app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_models.dart:24-31) doesn't even parse it — it isn't in the shared `AffiliateInfo` type either. The adjacent 'Wallet / Affiliate wallet' field (lines 104-110) is a plain div with a chevron icon that looks like a select but has no handler at all.
failure_scenario: Admin allocates an affiliate with 'Enable affiliate wallet access' switched OFF and confirms a dialog that says '…with a 5% commission rate' (wallet clause omitted). The affiliate nevertheless sees the affiliate wallet, the withdrawable balance and can submit a withdrawal request immediately. The admin also has no screen anywhere that shows the flag back, so the mistake is invisible.
fix: Either enforce `affiliate.walletEnabled` in requestWithdrawal (and hide the wallet on web/app when false, adding it to the shared AffiliateInfo type), or delete the toggle and the fake 'Wallet' field.

verdict.reason: Could not refute. `walletEnabled` from AllocateAffiliatePage.tsx:55/115 is persisted by adminAllocateAffiliate as `affiliate.walletEnabled` (functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:57) and read by nothing: a repo-wide grep across admin/, web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared and scripts/ returns only this page, the admin request type (admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts:61), the CF write itself (whose only "read" is its own carry-forward fallback), and the unrelated settings/paymentGateway.walletEnabled used by web checkout (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:239), Flutter checkout (app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:207) and PaymentGatewayTab. Every affiliate consumer gates on `affiliate.enabled` only: requestWithdrawal (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:36 `if (!aff?.enabled)`), web account/affiliate/page.tsx:90 and account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:84; the Flutter AffiliateInfo model (app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_models.dart:23-31) does not parse the field at all. So switching the toggle OFF still leaves the affiliate with full wallet/withdrawal access, while the confirm dialog (line 130) implies the choice matters, and no admin screen surfaces the flag afterwards. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry covers only the optional commissionRate) nor the known-intentional list; the CF comment "at least persist what the admin chose" concedes it is write-only. Real, fixable defect — either enforce it in requestWithdrawal/the customer surfaces or drop the toggle. Minor caveat: the adjacent "Wallet / Affiliate wallet" pseudo-select (lines 103-109) is genuinely cosmetic filler, but that is a side note, not the substance of the claim.

title: Firestore errors on the affiliate screen are swallowed — the page shows 'No withdrawal requests yet'
detail: `useLiveCollection` returns `{data, loading, error}` and sets `error` on the snapshot error callback (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts:113-117). AffiliateListPage destructures only `data`/`loading` at lines 36-37 and never renders the error, unlike every comparable screen (returns ReturnsListPage.tsx:37/106, subadmin SubAdminListPage.tsx:30/125, coupons, spinner). On error the data array stays `[]` and `loading` becomes false, so the table falls into the `withdrawals.length === 0` branch (line 157) and the stat cards render 0/₹0.
failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose Firebase custom claim hasn't propagated (or any permission-denied / missing-index / offline condition) opens Affiliate Program and sees '0 affiliates · ₹0 pending payout', four zeroed stat cards and 'No withdrawal requests yet.' They conclude nobody has requested a payout while real pending requests are sitting in Firestore, and nothing in the UI or a toast hints at a failure.
fix: Destructure `error` from both hooks and render the standard inline error banner (as ReturnsListPage does) instead of the empty state when `error && data.length === 0`.

verdict.reason: The core code fact holds: firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets {data: [], loading:false, error} on the snapshot error callback, and AffiliateListPage.tsx:36-37 destructures only data/loading, so a read error renders the 'No withdrawal requests yet.' branch (line 161) plus zeroed stat cards with no toast or banner. The repo explicitly treats this as a defect elsewhere (ReturnsListPage.tsx:105 'Read error — surfaced instead of a misleading empty state', SubAdminListPage.tsx:125, SpinnerListPage.tsx:89, CouponsListPage.tsx:51), and the fix is a small, established pattern on a money-critical screen. Two parts of the claim are overstated, however. (a) 'unlike every comparable screen' is false — CustomersListPage.tsx:19, OrdersListPage.tsx:26, PaymentsListPage.tsx:22 and ReviewsListPage.tsx:30 ignore `error` identically, so this is a shared gap, not an affiliate-specific outlier. (b) The stated trigger is mostly unreachable: firestore.rules:215 gates admins/{uid} on the role claim and initAuthListener (authStore.ts) catches a failed loadAdminDoc and signs the user out to /login, so an unpropagated sub-admin claim bounces to login rather than showing a silent affiliate page; plain offline does not fire the onSnapshot error callback, and both queries are indexed (indexes.json:100-107; affiliate.enabled == is single-field). Reachable triggers reduce to mid-session claim revocation (onAuthStateChanged does not re-fire on token refresh), a rules redeploy, or resource-exhausted. Real and fixable, but lower severity and less unique than claimed.

title: settings/affiliate is unmanageable from the admin panel; commission rates are a hardcoded 3/5/7/10 list
detail: `RATE_OPTIONS` is a hardcoded array and the form defaults to '5' without ever reading `settings/affiliate.defaultCommissionRate` — which the CF falls back to (functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:42) and which the admin already has a hook for: `useAffiliate()` in admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:25 is defined and never imported anywhere. There is no Affiliate tab in SettingsPage (VALID = variables/delivery/gateway/storefront/support/content, admin/src/features/settings/routes/SettingsPage.tsx:13), so `minWithdrawalPaise`, `processingFeeType/Value/MinPaise`, `maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise` and `defaultCommissionRate` — all read live by requestWithdrawal (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:25-28) and by the web withdraw screen — can only ever be set by re-running scripts/seed.ts or bootstrap-real.ts.
failure_scenario: Ops decides the minimum withdrawal should rise from ₹500 to ₹1,000 and the processing fee should become 1%. There is no screen in the admin panel to change either, so the values stay at whatever seed wrote; and an admin who wants to allocate an affiliate at 4% or 15% cannot — the dropdown only offers 3/5/7/10.
fix: Add an Affiliate settings tab wired to the existing `useAffiliate()` hook (default rate, min withdrawal, fee type/value/min, max per day) and seed RATE_OPTIONS / the default selection from `defaultCommissionRate`, or make the rate a free numeric percent input.

verdict.reason: Real, fixable gap. Verified: RATE_OPTIONS at admin/src/features/affiliate/routes/AllocateAffiliatePage.tsx:14 is a hardcoded 3/5/7/10 list with a '5' default and no settings read; useAffiliate() at admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:25 is defined and imported nowhere in admin/src; SettingsShell's SettingsTabId/SETTINGS_TABS have no affiliate tab and no AffiliateTab route file exists; the only writers of settings/affiliate in the repo are scripts/seed.ts:206 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:116. Meanwhile the doc is live-read in production by functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:24-28 (minWithdrawalPaise, processingFeeType/Value/MinPaise on every withdrawal), by functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts (defaultCommissionRate fallback), and by the web withdraw screen via useAffiliateSettings — so ops genuinely cannot change the minimum withdrawal or processing fee without re-running a seed script. firestore.rules:56 already allows canWrite('settings'), so nothing blocks a fix. Aggravating: the allocate screen filters to customers with !affiliate.enabled, so an existing affiliate's rate cannot be edited from admin at all. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry only made the CF accept an optional commissionRate, which is what makes arbitrary rates legal server-side) and not on the intentional list (that covers manual payouts / no bank API, not settings management). Two minor over-claims that do not change the verdict: maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise is read by no runtime code (dead config, only seed/bootstrap/type), and defaultCommissionRate is only a fallback since the admin form always sends an explicit rate.
